title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve Gender Equality? Evidence from a Natural Experiment
authors: Leo Bao; Difang Huang; Chen Lin
eligible_reason: Single adoption date. The AI-assisted revision intervention starts in month 6 for every student in the experiment group (data_main.dta: after = 1 for months 6-10 in both groups; all 136 treated students first treated in month 6), so treatment = after x experiment is a canonical two-group, single-date DiD. The at-least-two-cohorts rule fails. Main tables use reghdfe <outcome> after##experiment [x gender], absorb(month id class teacher); Table 2 column 1 is a fixed-effects logit (logitfe).
design_notes: Student-game panel of Go students at a training agency (22,382 games, 10 months). experiment = student in the treated group (teacher uses AI analysis), after = month >= 6. Table 2: quality, error, criticalerror, error_magnitude on after##experiment with month, id, class, teacher FE, cluster id; Tables 3+ add triple interaction with student gender (gender gap). Surveys (data_survey_cartoon.dta, data_survey_learning.dta) are cross-sectional.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Verified from data_main.dta: every treated student first has after = 1 in month 6.

specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date (month 6 for all treated students)
specs.notes: Cols 3-5 same for error, criticalerror, error_magnitude; col 1 logitfe.

screener_notes: Screened from package only (readme.pdf, table1-3.do, data_main.dta inspected for the after timing). No article text available.
